items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I called up to get a date there and Sonny said to me, “well come in on a Wednesday night, we have a jam session. If we like what you do we’ll give you a date.”

ctx.x: Somebody asked him, they said, “I’d like to take a lesson with you in improvisation.” And Chet, who is a little salty sometimes, said, “well improvisation is about imagination or lack of it.” So I always remembered that. You’d better have something to say, otherwise don’t say much. Say a little then get out. A long, long time ago I went to a jam session at a club in Seaford, Long Island called Sonny’s Place. It was a club that was there for many years and many great players and singers stopped in there just to…

another one.” I said, “yes indeed.” So to be accepted by somebody who I looked up to, I wouldn’t have cared if he threw me off the bandstand. Because that’s what they do. But to be accepted like that is like just huge for me. I mean I drove home, it was like a two hour drive home, I’m going like, “wow, Billy Mitchell said it was okay.” And then I got a gig, about three months later. He [Sonny] gave me a date that night, for three months down the road. And I showed up with a rhythm section with guys that I knew…
